findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). Instantiating an ABC with unimplemented abstracts raises TypeError. Detector.detector_handler does exactly that via group_type.detector_handler(self), and MetricAlertFire still sets detector_handler to this class. Previously this handler was concrete and evaluate() returned []. Any detector whose type resolves to metric_alert_fire will now crash when processed instead of no-opping.

findings.title: Group-key evaluation test expects the wrong occurrence
findings.body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence with group_key "val1" and value 6, then calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. build_occurrence_and_event_data uses that group_key in the fingerprint, so the occurrence the handler returns cannot equal the expected one (fingerprint "{detector_id}:val1" vs "{detector_id}:group_key"). This assertion fails, or if equality ignores fingerprint it does not actually check the occurrence the new hook produced.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], and process_detectors depends on .values(). The docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. Callers following the docstring will iterate the dict keys (group keys) instead of the results and mishandle evaluation output.
